RedWallet recovery, resilience, lifecycle and USDC refresh update

Opt-in recovery searches Native SegWit (BIP84) and Taproot (BIP86), accounts 0–2 or 0–9, receive and change branches, with 20 or 100 unused-address gaps. Spent-out history counts. Recovery reports incomplete scans on server errors or limits. Public-account imports search only that account; discovery requires your configured XBT server. No finite search guarantees every address or account.

Optional TLS backup servers: up to five, tested before saving and verified against the XBT checkpoint. No automatic public server or plaintext downgrade. Servers see address queries; checkpoint verification is not full SPV.

Encryption preserves transaction history; failed cache migration preserves the original storage. Deleted wallets clear their active cache. Red splash/loading and receive QR artwork replace inherited blue assets. Transaction-history and batch-limit fixes are retained.

Fresh isolated Knots tests accepted SegWit and Taproot sends, RBF and CPFP and confirmed the resulting transactions. Software tests cover recovery, refresh, signing, encrypted restart, wrong-password rejection, deletion and recovery. Physical-device and live Fulcrum interoperability testing remain separate.

Includes XBT Unified signing, watch-only imports and signed-PSBT cold signing. External signers must support Unified 0x21. Taproot key-path only; no annex/script paths or multisig. RBF needs sufficient change; CPFP supports one unconfirmed parent. After restart, create a fresh signing request.

USDC estimates display two decimals; XBT coin amounts retain full precision. Saved NeoxEX quotes refresh on app launch and foreground return, recalculate the total, and retain the last valid quote if offline. Manual prices stay unchanged.

Update the existing app, then refresh the existing wallet.
